q: Nadia: 'People seem to be quitting the Spanish course.' First move?
o: Climb the ladder: goal and decision first

q: Before: 75% organic at 35% and 25% paid at 15%. Week-4 retention in %?
After: 55% organic at 35% and 45% paid at 15%. Week-4 retention in %?
Neither channel's retention changed. What explains the drop?
why: The share of lower-retention paid learners grew.

q: Lesson 6 has a 40% quit rate, and had it last quarter too. What is it?
o: The cause of this quarter's drop
A separate, older leak worth fixing
why: It didn't cause the drop, but it's the biggest leak.

q: 20,000 learners reach lesson 6. Quit rate falls from 40% to 25%. How many more learners stay?
Which guardrail fits a targeting change for the Spanish ads?
o: New Spanish learners per week mustn't drop past an agreed amount
why: Better targeting may bring fewer, better learners; agree the limit first.

q: When should the follow-up be measured?
o: 30 days after release, outside promotions, channel mix held constant
why: A clean window, so neither a sale nor a mix shift can fake a win.

q: Since the drop is all mix shift, there's nothing for the content team to do.
why: Myth. Lesson 6 is still the biggest leak in the biggest course.

q: Which depth did the Spanish question need?
o: An initial exploration that answered it
why: It answered the decision; a one-week content change needs no deep dive.
